items.followUp: Name the four major types of biomolecules and give one example of each.

rubric.why: Checks identification of biomolecule types with examples.
rubric.description: Names two biomolecule types and gives a correct example for each.
rubric.how: Award ½ mark for each correct type-example pair.

rubric.why: Checks two further correct biomolecule type-example pairs.
rubric.description: Names two further biomolecule types and gives a correct example for each.
rubric.how: Award ½ mark for each correct type-example pair.

modelAnswer: The four major types of biomolecules are carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.
Carbohydrate: glucose; protein: enzyme; lipid: fat; nucleic acid: DNA.

items.followUp: Name two books written by Abdul Malik Asmai.

rubric.why: Checks knowledge of books attributed to Abdul Malik Asmai.
rubric.description: Gives the names of two books written by Abdul Malik Asmai.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correct book title.

modelAnswer: Abdul Malik Asmai wrote books including Al-Khail (on horses), Al-Ibil (on camels), Al-Shat (on sheep), Al-Wuhush (on wild animals) and Khalq-ul-Insan.

items.followUp: Name two kinds of plant tissues and two kinds of animal tissues.

rubric.why: Checks examples of plant tissue types.
rubric.description: Names two types of plant tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct plant tissue types.

rubric.why: Checks examples of animal tissue types.
rubric.description: Names two types of animal tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct animal tissue types.

modelAnswer: Plant tissues: meristematic tissue and permanent tissue.
Animal tissues: epithelial tissue and connective tissue.

items.followUp: How did Ronald Ross show that mosquitoes transmit malaria?

rubric.why: Checks King's observation linking malaria with places where mosquitoes breed.
rubric.description: States that malaria was associated with marshy or swampy places where mosquitoes were common.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking malaria with marshes/swamps or mosquitoes.

rubric.why: Checks the inference that mosquitoes spread malaria.
rubric.description: States that malaria is transmitted through the bite of an infected mosquito.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the mosquito-borne transmission observation.

modelAnswer: A.F.A. King observed that malaria was common in marshy places where mosquitoes bred.
He concluded that mosquitoes could be involved in spreading malaria; the disease is transmitted by the bite of an infected mosquito.

items.followUp: What are the functions of red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets?

rubric.why: Checks the principal transport role of red blood cells.
rubric.description: States that red blood cells carry oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the oxygen-transport function.

rubric.why: Checks the defensive role of white blood cells and the clotting role of platelets.
rubric.description: States that white blood cells defend the body against infection and/or platelets help clot blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct function; award the mark only once.

modelAnswer: Red blood cells transport oxygen to body tissues.
White blood cells defend the body against disease-causing organisms.
Platelets help clot the blood and prevent excessive bleeding.

items.followUp: Why are viruses not placed in any of the five kingdoms?

rubric.why: Checks the non-cellular nature of viruses.
rubric.description: States that viruses are acellular or lack cellular structure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the acellular nature of viruses.

rubric.why: Checks their unusual status in classification.
rubric.description: Explains that viruses show both living and non-living characteristics and are not included in the five-kingdom classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for their unclassified, borderline status.

modelAnswer: Viruses are acellular and show both living and non-living characteristics.
Therefore, they are not placed in any of the five kingdoms.

items.followUp: Which of the five kingdoms contains prokaryotic organisms, and which contain eukaryotic organisms?

rubric.why: Checks identification of the prokaryotic kingdom.
rubric.description: Identifies Monera as the prokaryotic kingdom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming Monera and its cell type.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the eukaryotic kingdoms.
rubric.description: Identifies Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia as eukaryotic kingdoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the four eukaryotic kingdoms.

modelAnswer: The kingdom Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms.
The kingdoms Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia consist of eukaryotic organisms.

items.followUp: How does meiosis help maintain the chromosome number in a species over generations?

rubric.why: Checks the reduction in chromosome number during meiosis.
rubric.description: States that meiosis produces haploid cells or halves the chromosome number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the reduction to the haploid number.

rubric.why: Checks how meiosis and fertilization preserve chromosome number across generations.
rubric.description: Explains that fertilization restores the diploid number, keeping the species' chromosome number constant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking fertilization with restoration or maintenance of chromosome number.

modelAnswer: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and produces haploid gametes.
At fertilization, two haploid gametes fuse and restore the diploid chromosome number.
Thus, the chromosome number remains constant from one generation to the next.
